h1: The 6 Best Ultrasonic Cleaner Solutions of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 ultrasonic cleaner solutions scored on dilution, yield and material safety, from jewelry formulas to engine-part degreasers.
summary: WoldoClean is the best all-round solution, a non-toxic, ammonia-free concentrate that makes 8 gallons and suits eyeglasses, dental items and small parts. The Sylvan Hills 32 oz stretches furthest, mixing at 1 to 250 for up to 50 gallons of engine-part cleaner. Jewelry owners should buy the iSonic or Blitz, and Qucship is the refill for big tanks.
intro: The most expensive mistake in ultrasonic cleaning is using the wrong liquid. Plain water cleans surface dust but leaves oil alone, and a heavy engine degreaser will cloud a lens coating or etch soft gemstones. The solution is not interchangeable, and the label rarely says what it will damage.

We ranked six concentrates by what matters when you pour: dilution ratio, gallons per bottle, which materials the maker names and which it warns against. Scores follow the Primea framework. The result splits cleanly into household formulas for glasses and jewelry, and heavier concentrates for carburetors and metal parts.

products.name: WoldoClean Ultrasonic Cleaner Solution Concentrate, 25.4 oz
products.verdict: A gentle ammonia-free concentrate that makes 8 gallons for glasses, dental items and razors.
products.description:
WoldoClean sells 25.4 fl oz of concentrate that dilutes at 1 to 40 to make 8 gallons. You add one capful in warm water, and it fits machines from 8 to 64 fl oz. The formula is non-toxic and ammonia free, which matters because ammonia can attack lens coatings.

It wins because it covers the most household jobs with one bottle: eyeglasses, dental items, razors and small parts. The iSonic is similar for glasses and jewelry but names fewer item types, and the Blitz is for jewelry only. Neither lists a gallon yield.

Buy it if you own one tabletop cleaner and want one bottle for everything. The caveat is that it is not a heavy degreaser, so engine parts need the Sylvan Hills or Qucship.
products.idealFor: Households cleaning glasses, dental items and razors.
products.skipIf: You rebuild carburetors or clean greasy engine parts.

products.name: Sylvan Hills 32 oz Ultrasonic Carburetor and Parts Cleaner
products.verdict: Mixes at 1 to 250, so one 32 oz bottle stretches to 50 gallons.
products.description:
Sylvan Hills sells a 32 oz concentrate that mixes at 1 to 250 with water, producing up to 50 gallons. It is listed for aluminum, brass, copper and steel, and a microfiber cloth is included.

It ranks second because no other bottle here goes so far: at 1 to 250 the dilution is six times more diluted than the WoldoClean's 1 to 40, so the cost per gallon is the lowest in the group. The Qucship beats it on bottle size, but needs a stronger mix for the same job.

Buy it if you clean small engine parts often. The caveat is that a 1 to 250 mix is only as good as your measuring, so use a graduated cylinder, not a guess.
products.idealFor: DIY mechanics cleaning small engine parts often.
products.skipIf: You want a gentle formula for eyewear or gems.

products.name: Qucship Ultrasonic Carburetor Cleaner, Makes 9 Gallons
products.verdict: A 128 oz gallon of 8x concentrate with the widest metals list.
products.description:
Qucship ships a 128 oz (one gallon) bottle of 8x concentrate that makes 9 gallons. The listing names aluminum, copper, zinc, iron, steel, magnesium and brass, and also mentions plastic parts and coins.

It ranks third because 9 gallons is far less than Sylvan Hills' 50 gallons, though the bottle is four times larger. The advantage here is the metals list: zinc and magnesium are soft, reactive metals that many cleaners warn against, so having them named is useful in a carburetor or die-cast job.

Buy it if you refill a large tank often. The caveat is the mention of plastic parts and coins, which is not a promise of safety, so test on a hidden part first.
products.idealFor: Shops and hobbyists refilling a large tank.
products.skipIf: You only run a small jewelry tub.

products.name: iSonic Jewelry and Eyeglass Cleaner Solution Concentrate
products.verdict: A professional-style concentrate for gold, silver, diamonds, watches and eyewear.
products.description:
iSonic's concentrate is dosed at one capful per use and is intended for gold, silver, diamond, watches and eyewear. It is non-toxic, biodegradable and American-made.

It ranks fourth because it publishes no gallon yield or dilution ratio, so cost per use is hard to compare with the WoldoClean, which states 8 gallons at 1 to 40. Where it earns its place is specificity: naming watches and diamonds tells you the maker has thought about these items, rather than selling a general soap.

Buy it for a jewelry box and a pair of glasses. The caveat is that you should keep it away from soft stones such as pearls and opals, which no ultrasonic cleaner handles well.
products.idealFor: Jewelry and eyeglass owners who want a gentle concentrate.
products.skipIf: You compare solutions by cost per gallon.

products.name: Tillbrook Ultrasonic Cleaner Solution, Makes 8 Gallons
products.verdict: A focused auto-parts concentrate for dirt, varnish and gums.
products.description:
Tillbrook makes 8 gallons of auto-parts cleaner from a concentrated formula, aimed at carburetors, injection parts and metals. It targets dirt, varnish and gums, the sticky residues left by old fuel, and it is made in the USA.

It ranks fifth because the Sylvan Hills and Qucship both publish more detail: the first lists a 1 to 250 mix and four metals, the second lists seven metals. Tillbrook states a yield and a target, but not a ratio or a metals list, so you need to match it to your parts yourself.

Buy it if you are rebuilding a carburetor and want a focused product. It sits in the $25 to $50 bracket, the same as the Qucship.
products.idealFor: Hobby mechanics rebuilding carburetors and injectors.
products.skipIf: You need a stated mix ratio or metals list.

products.name: Blitz Gem and Jewelry Cleaner Concentrate Refill, 8 oz
products.verdict: A small jewelry-only refill from a brand dating to 1912.
products.description:
Blitz sells an 8 oz concentrate that stretches to eight times its volume. It is nontoxic, non-abrasive and biodegradable, aimed at diamonds, emeralds, jewelry and accessories, and the brand dates to 1912.

It ranks last because it is the narrowest product here: jewelry only, with no eyewear or watch mention, and no stated gallon yield. Against the iSonic it is simpler and cheaper, and emeralds are named, though emeralds are often treated stones that dealers warn about in ultrasonic baths, so check with a jeweler first.

Buy it if you clean rings and chains in a small tub. Skip it for glasses, tools or engine parts.
products.idealFor: People cleaning only rings and chains.
products.skipIf: You also clean glasses, tools or engine parts.

methodology.description: Mix ratio and gallons per bottle set the real cost per cleaning, more than the bottle price.

methodology.title: Formula chemistry
methodology.description: Ammonia-free, non-toxic and biodegradable claims affect safety for lenses, hands and drains.

methodology.title: Cleaning target
methodology.description: Whether the formula aims at skin oil, varnish or grease decides if it suits the job.

methodology.title: Value and bottle size

whatMatters.detail: The ratio tells you how many parts water per part concentrate. A 1 to 250 mix, like the Sylvan Hills, goes much further than a 1 to 40 mix, like the WoldoClean. It matters because cost per gallon, not bottle price, is the real cost. Check the listing for a ratio and use a measuring cup.

Ultrasonic action is harmless to hard materials, but chemistry is not. Some solutions attack soft metals such as zinc and magnesium, or coatings on lenses. Qucship names seven metals; WoldoClean names lens-safe use. Check that your item appears in the listing, and test on a hidden spot.

Ammonia cleans well but damages anti-reflective lens coatings and some plastics. An ammonia-free label, as on WoldoClean, is the safer default for eyeglasses. Look for the words ammonia free on the listing, and avoid ammonia products for lenses, watches and coated jewelry.

A concentrate is mixed to the tank's volume, so a small jewelry tub uses a capful, while a 6 L tank needs more. WoldoClean states 8 to 64 fl oz machines. Check your tank capacity before buying, and note whether the bottle suits refilling a tank or a single use.

Skin oil and polish residue need a mild soap, while varnish and gums from old fuel need a stronger degreaser. Tillbrook names varnish and gums; iSonic names gold and diamonds. Match the target soil on the listing to what is on your part.

faq.q: Can I use any solution in any ultrasonic cleaner?
faq.a: Tank material and heater matter. WoldoClean states 8 to 64 fl oz machines. Strong degreasers like Sylvan Hills should go in a stainless tank, not a plastic jewelry tub, so check your machine manual.

faq.q: What mistake do people make most often?
faq.a: Using engine cleaner on lenses or jewelry. Qucship and Tillbrook target metals and grime, and can damage coatings. Keep a household bottle like WoldoClean or iSonic for personal items.

faq.q: Is the Sylvan Hills worth it over the Qucship?
faq.a: If you want the lowest cost per gallon, yes: 1 to 250 gives up to 50 gallons. The Qucship offers a bigger bottle and seven named metals, but makes only 9 gallons.

faq.q: How do I mix a concentrate?
faq.a: Measure the concentrate first, then add warm water to the tank's line. For WoldoClean, one capful goes in per tank, and for Sylvan Hills, mix 1 part to 250 parts water.

faq.q: How long does a mixed solution last?
faq.a: Replace it when it looks dark or cloudy. Engine solutions fill with residue faster than the iSonic or Blitz jewelry mixes, so change them after each heavy job.

faq.q: Can I use these on pearls or opals?
faq.a: No. Soft or porous stones can be damaged by ultrasonic action itself. Even gentle formulas like Blitz or iSonic are meant for hard stones such as diamonds, so ask a jeweler about treated gems.

finalTake: WoldoClean is the bottle most households should own: ammonia free, 8 gallons per bottle and safe on the things people actually clean. Buy the Sylvan Hills for engine parts, because 1 to 250 dilution is hard to beat, and the Qucship if your tank is large. Pick iSonic for a jewelry box. Match the formula to the item, then measure the mix.
